about.title: Salinas Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in Salinas is supposed to make things better. When it doesn't—when a diagnosis is missed at a Monterey County clinic, a surgery goes wrong, or a medication error sends someone back to the emergency room—families are often left guessing about what happened. That uncertainty is where a medical malpractice claim begins. One thing matters up front: a poor result by itself is not malpractice. California law asks whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care, and proving that almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review the records and explain what should have been done differently. Salinas is home to roughly 157,380 people, and in 2025 alone its roads saw 560 people injured in collisions—many of them passing through the same hospitals and urgent-care rooms where treatment mistakes can occur. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Salinas residents, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can learn whether your situation is worth pursuing before you owe anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Salinas Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA deadlines are short and unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury—and never more than three years from when it occurred—plus a 90-day pre-suit notice must go out first. Getting connected early protects that window.

items.title: Expert review is built into the process
items.desc: Nearly every malpractice case requires a qualified medical expert to establish that care fell below the standard. The attorneys in our network know how to arrange that review before filing, not after.

items.title: Honest talk about what the cap means
items.desc: MICRA limits non-economic damages, though the cap rises each year. An independent attorney will explain how that applies to your situation without inflating expectations or promising a number.

items.question: I was treated in Salinas but later transferred to a hospital outside Monterey County. Does that change my claim?
items.answer: It can, but it doesn't disqualify you. Which providers may be responsible depends on where the error occurred and who was involved, and an attorney will typically request records from every facility in the chain. Claims involving Salinas care often proceed in Monterey County, though your attorney will sort out the correct venue based on the facts.

items.question: How is malpractice different from a bad outcome?
items.answer: Medicine carries risk, and a treatment that fails is not automatically negligent. Malpractice means a provider did something a reasonably careful provider would not have done—or failed to do something they should have. That gap is what a qualified medical expert must identify, and without it a claim generally cannot move forward.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery, and the initial evaluation carries no obligation.
